newsitem.title: USA: USDA to help get feed to snowbound Dakotas cattle.
newsitem.headline: USDA to help get feed to snowbound Dakotas cattle.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Thursday moved to help get feed to 100,000 head of livestock stranded by blizzards in the Northern Plains by activating an emergency feed grain donation program.

USDA said it would provide feed grains from its disaster reserve or use funds from the sale of reserve grain to help buy livestock feed to be shipped into stricken areas or to allow producers to buy feed locally when available.
USDA said the funds may also be used for transporting grain and removing snow to feed cattle.
The estimated cost of feeding the 100,000 head for 15 days will be about $1.4 million and USDA said it will foot the bill due to the "severity of the problem."
The department said for longer range assistance, producers will have to provide 70 percent of the cost of feed acquired under the disaster reserve assistance program.
USDA said it surveyed the warehouses in the area and found almost 600,000 bushels of corn, barley and wheat that could be used immediately.

It said South Dakota has about 80,000 head at immediate risk. In North Dakota, about 20,000 head are at immediate risk and producers will soon exhaust hay supplies. Cattle stranded away from feed sources are expected to be a problem for the next several months, USDA said.
